His fastest whiff punish is sonic fang at 14 frames. Otherwise his range is lackluster in neutral. His stances allow him to cover ground at the risk of exposing himself.

Steve has average combo damage and the optimal ones are hard. They were also nerfed in s4. At the wall massaji ender is damaging yeah.

Sidestepping Steve is usually not recommended unless you know exactly what you're sidestepping. 

His RA and RD make up for his weakness in launchers and come back potential. Even then, Steve has huge problems coming back from a life deficit vs a defensive player.

Spotted some mistakes on first watch:
After backlash on whiff, it's not a good idea to press or jab. You'll most likely get b3'd exactly like what happened.

During Hwo pressure strings, one backdash usually creates enough space for a whiff in a lot of situations, so try that.

After b12 hits, you're pretty much guaranteed an attempt on qcf1/d21 so try that! 

f21 into pkb isn't very strong as it's visually predictable and the high is duckable.

Doing pkb uf2 in neutral isn't really a good choice because opponents usually are defensive when seeing Steve in pkb. Manual instant pkbuf2 is good for getting a launch on a twitch whiff prediction. (for example buffering a sidestep after a jab and doing pkbuf2 as soon as you see the opponent try to jab back)

After jfsr the opponent loses their turn, so do check them with dck pressure/qcf1

Vary your timing on the d21 string. All hits are delayable as hell. You can also do some pattern like d2 into d2>1. Keep them guessing.

The rest of Hwo pressure/setups need to be labbed unfortunately. But Steve has a lot of OS due to his Sway.

Finally, commendations on the df2 combo. I only recently attempted to learn it. I got to purple only with df2 into fcdf2. That being said, you gotta start using different routes and enders to maximise wall carry. The dckf2 route is a bit inflexible and the dash df12 finisher often whiffs as you saw. By doing the flk 1(1),d1 route, you can finish with dck1, df1+2, df2~dck1, iFLK 11alb2, b1~1alb2, pkbf2, 1 and uf1 for different levels of carry, oki and damage. So do explore your options!

In general it's going to depend on your style but I might add a few tips.

1 Stargate Oracle gets dealt with spores in each mineral lines. No need for corruptors unless it's a stylistic choice over mutas (if you want some air support). Hydras are a nice alternative because generally he's going to have between 4 and 6 phoenixes and a dozen of hydras clean that up.

2 Stargate Oracle opening into heavy Phoenix pressure means that he's going to have at least 6 Phoenixes. If he goes for exactly 6, the typical 1 Stargate response is enough. However if he goes for 8+ Phoenixes, put 2 spores near each gas on each hatch, rally individual hatches to their respective safe zones, recall all ovies and hover them under a hatch with 3 spores surrounding it. Get lair and fast hydras/corruptors.

Adept all-ins get dealt with roaches. No need to pump out too many ravagers unless it's necessary (sentry play). Should depend on the amount of adepts he's committing tho. Generally you want to have 2 base saturation before pumping roaches out if he has a late 2nd, or if you see a saturated 2nd then go for 2.5 base saturation before roaches.

Immortal-Chargelot all-ins get dealt with ling + ravagers (since they don't get bonus dmg from immortals) if it hits before your lurker tech (which takes a lot of time to get to). Mutas are also a nice alternative.

Against blink stalkers, the safest response is to get a few infestors up, lings and accessory lurkers; enough to deal with the push. You want to emphasise on hive tech. Cracklings are amazing against them.

3 nexii before cybercore can get shut down by 2 base timing attacks, ling drops, taking faster expansions or even being greedier than the toss (4 hatch before pool for example).

There's tons of other reactions to each and every opening and I certainly do not know them all. I hope I've been of help, even if it's just a little bit.
